a five-station obstacle course in MuJoCo using\n\u003cstrong\u003eonly its onboard camera\u003c/strong\u003e. A small judgment model (\u003ca href=\"https://typesafe.ai\" rel=\"nofollow\"\u003eTypeSafe\u003c/a\u003e's\nJev) sits at ~2.5 Hz and decides \u003cem\u003ewhat the situation means\u003c/em\u003e; everything\ntime-critical stays in ordinary code.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ca target=\"_blank\" rel=\"noopener noreferrer\" href=\"/RomanSlack/jev-drone/blob/main/docs/climb.png\"\u003e\u003cimg src=\"/RomanSlack/jev-drone/raw/main/docs/climb.png\" alt=\"climbing over a barrier\" style=\"max-width: 100%;\"\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eThe drone is the Skydio X2 from \u003ca href=\"https://github.com/google-deepmind/mujoco_menagerie\"\u003eMuJoCo Menagerie\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cul dir=\"auto\"\u003e\n\u003cli\u003ea real airframe with four rotors, flown by a geometric controller. Nothing\nabout the flight is scripted.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"markdown-heading\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ch2 tabindex=\"-1\" class=\"heading-element\" dir=\"auto\"\u003eThe idea\u003c/h2\u003e\u003ca id=\"user-content-the-idea\" class=\"anchor\" aria-label=\"Permalink: The idea\" href=\"#the-idea\"\u003e\u003csvg data-component=\"Octicon\" class=\"octicon octicon-link\" viewBox=\"0 0 16 16\" version=\"1.1\" width=\"16\" height=\"16\" aria-hidden=\"true\"\u003e\u003cpath d=\"m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z\"\u003e\u003c/path\u003e\u003c/svg\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eJev is \u003cstrong\u003enot\u003c/strong\u003e a vision model. It takes JSON and returns typed answers with\nprobabilities. So it cannot be the perception layer, and it cannot run at\ncontrol rate. What it can do is answer small questions about a situation that\nordinary code finds hard to phrase.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"snippet-clipboard-content notranslate position-relative overflow-auto\" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content=\" 500 Hz   geometric controller       flight.Pilot    thrust-priority mixing, slew-limited\n  50 Hz   guidance + safety reflex   run.Guidance    ALWAYS owns safety\n  15 Hz   camera -\u0026gt; symbolic scene   flight.Eye      depth + segmentation, no ground truth\n~2.5 Hz   tactical judgment          tactics.py      Jev, advisory only\"\u003e\u003cpre class=\"notranslate\"\u003e\u003ccode\u003e 500 Hz   geometric controller       flight.Pilot    thrust-priority mixing, slew-limited\n  50 Hz   guidance + safety reflex   run.Guidance    ALWAYS owns safety\n  15 Hz   camera -\u0026gt; symbolic scene   flight.Eye      depth + segmentation, no ground truth\n~2.5 Hz   tactical judgment          tactics.py      Jev, advisory only\n\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/pre\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eClassical CV turns the depth and segmentation buffers into a compact scene:\nfive forward range sectors, the height of whatever is blocking the path,\nwhether its top edge is even visible, and where the target is. Jev reads that\nand answers three questions in one call:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cmarkdown-accessiblity-table\u003e\u003ctable\u003e\n\u003cthead\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003cth\u003equestion\u003c/th\u003e\n\u003cth\u003etype\u003c/th\u003e\n\u003cth\u003eoptions\u003c/th\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003c/thead\u003e\n\u003ctbody\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003emaneuver\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eChoice\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003ehold_course / gap_left / gap_right / climb / brake / reacquire\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003erisk\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eScore\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eclear and open -\u0026gt; tight -\u0026gt; about to hit something\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003etarget_truly_lost\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eNoul\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003egenuinely lost, or just briefly occluded?\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003c/tbody\u003e\n\u003c/table\u003e\u003c/markdown-accessiblity-table\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eCode decides \u003cem\u003ewhen\u003c/em\u003e to ask. On an open corridor with the target in view there\nis nothing to decide, so no call is made. Scenes are fingerprinted so an\nunchanged situation reuses the last judgment. A typical 65 s flight costs about\n110 calls.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eCode keeps the veto.\u003c/strong\u003e A hard reflex layer runs at 50 Hz and overrides any\njudgment when something is close. Jev can propose \u003ccode\u003eclimb\u003c/code\u003e, but code refuses it\nunless the obstruction's measured top edge is actually within the aircraft's\nclimb ceiling.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"markdown-heading\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ch2 tabindex=\"-1\" class=\"heading-element\" dir=\"auto\"\u003eThe course\u003c/h2\u003e\u003ca id=\"user-content-the-course\" class=\"anchor\" aria-label=\"Permalink: The course\" href=\"#the-course\"\u003e\u003csvg data-component=\"Octicon\" class=\"octicon octicon-link\" viewBox=\"0 0 16 16\" version=\"1.1\" width=\"16\" height=\"16\" aria-hidden=\"true\"\u003e\u003cpath d=\"m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z\"\u003e\u003c/path\u003e\u003c/svg\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eFive stations, each breaking a different assumption:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003col dir=\"auto\"\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eSlalom\u003c/strong\u003e - ordinary steering around pillars\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eLow beam\u003c/strong\u003e - spans the whole corridor. No lateral gap exists at any width, so \"go around\" is not available. It must be flown \u003cem\u003eover\u003c/em\u003e.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eTurnstiles\u003c/strong\u003e - arms sweeping across the lane. Moving, must be timed.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eSliding gate\u003c/strong\u003e - a 3.2 m gap that slides sideways. Too tall to climb, so it must be threaded.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eCluster\u003c/strong\u003e - dense pillars\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ol\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ca target=\"_blank\" rel=\"noopener noreferrer\" href=\"/RomanSlack/jev-drone/blob/main/docs/chase.png\"\u003e\u003cimg src=\"/RomanSlack/jev-drone/raw/main/docs/chase.png\" alt=\"chasing through the course\" style=\"max-width: 100%;\"\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"markdown-heading\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ch2 tabindex=\"-1\" class=\"heading-element\" dir=\"auto\"\u003eResults\u003c/h2\u003e\u003ca id=\"user-content-results\" class=\"anchor\" aria-label=\"Permalink: Results\" href=\"#results\"\u003e\u003csvg data-component=\"Octicon\" class=\"octicon octicon-link\" viewBox=\"0 0 16 16\" version=\"1.1\" width=\"16\" height=\"16\" aria-hidden=\"true\"\u003e\u003cpath d=\"m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z\"\u003e\u003c/path\u003e\u003c/svg\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eThe ablation is the same stack with the Jev call disabled, falling back to a\ngreedy \"steer toward the wider side\" heuristic. That baseline is \u003cem\u003esafe but\nstuck\u003c/em\u003e: it never crashes and it never gets past station 2, because going over\nan obstacle is not something it can express.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cmarkdown-accessiblity-table\u003e\u003ctable\u003e\n\u003cthead\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003cth\u003e\u003c/th\u003e\n\u003cth\u003ebaseline (no Jev)\u003c/th\u003e\n\u003cth\u003eJev engaged\u003c/th\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003c/thead\u003e\n\u003ctbody\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003efurthest point reached\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e17.7 / 17.7 / 17.7 m\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003cstrong\u003e77.5 m (whole course)\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003etarget kept in view\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e~19%\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003cstrong\u003e82%\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003etime pinned in reflex\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e65-71%\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003cstrong\u003e9%\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003ecollisions\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e0 / 0 / 0\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003cstrong\u003e0\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003c/tbody\u003e\n\u003c/table\u003e\u003c/markdown-accessiblity-table\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eThe baseline stops dead at station 2 every single time. With Jev the drone\nclears the entire course in about 47 s at up to 3.6 m/s:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"snippet-clipboard-content notranslate position-relative overflow-auto\" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content=\"x=19  beam0       t=15.7  z=3.0   climbed over\nx=26  turnstiles  t=20.3  z=1.6   timed the sweeping arms\nx=38  GATE        t=31.3  z=1.6   threaded the sliding 3.2 m gap\nx=44  beam1       t=36.8  z=2.8   climbed over\nx=50  cluster     t=41.3  z=1.6   lost the rover in the pillars\nx=58  exit        t=46.6          re-acquired it and closed back to 3.7 m\"\u003e\u003cpre class=\"notranslate\"\u003e\u003ccode\u003ex=19  beam0       t=15.7  z=3.0   climbed over\nx=26  turnstiles  t=20.3  z=1.6   timed the sweeping arms\nx=38  GATE        t=31.3  z=1.6   threaded the sliding 3.2 m gap\nx=44  beam1       t=36.8  z=2.8   climbed over\nx=50  cluster     t=41.3  z=1.6   lost the rover in the pillars\nx=58  exit        t=46.6          re-acquired it and closed back to 3.7 m\n\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/pre\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ca target=\"_blank\" rel=\"noopener noreferrer\" href=\"/RomanSlack/jev-drone/blob/main/docs/gate.png\"\u003e\u003cimg src=\"/RomanSlack/jev-drone/raw/main/docs/gate.png\" alt=\"threading the sliding gate\" style=\"max-width: 100%;\"\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e80 calls over 65 s, 0.11 s median latency, 96k tokens.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eThe cluster is worth noting: the drone genuinely loses the rover there, flies to\nwhere it estimates the rover has got to, and picks it back up. That recovery is\nthe difference between a demo and a system.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eHonest caveats.\u003c/strong\u003e The Jev column is a single 65 s run, not a seed-matched\naverage. On an earlier, simpler arena a matched 3-seed comparison showed \u003cstrong\u003eno\nadvantage\u003c/strong\u003e for Jev (it crossed 0/3, same as baseline) - the extra maneuvering\ncost target visibility. Run-to-run variance is large. The claim this repo\nsupports is narrow and specific: \u003cem\u003ethe baseline is structurally incapable of the\nmaneuver, and Jev supplies it.\u003c/em\u003e It is not \"the model makes the drone better at\neverything\".\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"markdown-heading\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ch3 tabindex=\"-1\" class=\"heading-element\" dir=\"auto\"\u003eWhat is and is not the model\u003c/h3\u003e\u003ca id=\"user-content-what-is-and-is-not-the-model\" class=\"anchor\" aria-label=\"Permalink: What is and is not the model\" href=\"#what-is-and-is-not-the-model\"\u003e\u003csvg data-component=\"Octicon\" class=\"octicon octicon-link\" viewBox=\"0 0 16 16\" version=\"1.1\" width=\"16\" height=\"16\" aria-hidden=\"true\"\u003e\u003cpath d=\"m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z\"\u003e\u003c/path\u003e\u003c/svg\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eWorth being precise, because it is easy to overclaim:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cmarkdown-accessiblity-table\u003e\u003ctable\u003e\n\u003cthead\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003cth\u003elayer\u003c/th\u003e\n\u003cth\u003ewho does it\u003c/th\u003e\n\u003cth\u003erate\u003c/th\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003c/thead\u003e\n\u003ctbody\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eAwareness\u003c/strong\u003e - what is out there, how far, where is the target\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003enumpy on depth + segmentation. \u003cstrong\u003eZero Jev.\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e15 Hz\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eFlight control - attitude, thrust, mixing\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003egeometric controller. \u003cstrong\u003eZero Jev.\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e500 Hz\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eSafety reflex - do not hit that\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003ecode, and it \u003cstrong\u003eoverrides\u003c/strong\u003e Jev\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e50 Hz\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eTactical choice\u003c/strong\u003e - over it? around it? which side? is it lost?\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003cstrong\u003e100% Jev\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e~3 Hz\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003c/tbody\u003e\n\u003c/table\u003e\u003c/markdown-accessiblity-table\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eCode decides \u003cem\u003ewhat is there\u003c/em\u003e; Jev decides \u003cem\u003ewhat to do about it\u003c/em\u003e. Jev cannot see\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cul dir=\"auto\"\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eit takes JSON, not pixels. The defensible claim is \"a judgment model in a\nlive control loop at 3 Hz with 0.11 s median latency\", not \"the model does the\nperception\".\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"markdown-heading\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ch3 tabindex=\"-1\" class=\"heading-element\" dir=\"auto\"\u003eThe judgments themselves are good\u003c/h3\u003e\u003ca id=\"user-content-the-judgments-themselves-are-good\" class=\"anchor\" aria-label=\"Permalink: The judgments themselves are good\" href=\"#the-judgments-themselves-are-good\"\u003e\u003csvg data-component=\"Octicon\" class=\"octicon octicon-link\" viewBox=\"0 0 16 16\" version=\"1.1\" width=\"16\" height=\"16\" aria-hidden=\"true\"\u003e\u003cpath d=\"m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z\"\u003e\u003c/path\u003e\u003c/svg\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eOn hand-built scenes, 6 of 7 correct with strong probabilities:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"snippet-clipboard-content notranslate position-relative overflow-auto\" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content=\"LOW BARRIER, all 5 blocked, top 0.45m  -\u0026gt; climb        p=0.93  risk=1.42\nTALL PILLAR ahead, right wide open     -\u0026gt; gap_right    p=0.72  risk=1.53\nTALL PILLAR ahead, left wide open      -\u0026gt; gap_left     p=0.40  risk=1.58\nTARGET GONE 7s, wide open              -\u0026gt; reacquire    p=0.96  lost=0.85\nBOXED IN, close on all sides, tall     -\u0026gt; brake        p=0.84  risk=1.89\nALL CLEAR, target dead ahead           -\u0026gt; hold_course  p=0.82  risk=0.46\nBRIEF OCCLUSION 0.6s, path clear       -\u0026gt; (muddy, p=0.24)      lost=0.12\"\u003e\u003cpre class=\"notranslate\"\u003e\u003ccode\u003eLOW BARRIER, all 5 blocked, top 0.45m  -\u0026gt; climb        p=0.93  risk=1.42\nTALL PILLAR ahead, right wide open     -\u0026gt; gap_right    p=0.72  risk=1.53\nTALL PILLAR ahead, left wide open      -\u0026gt; gap_left     p=0.40  risk=1.58\nTARGET GONE 7s, wide open              -\u0026gt; reacquire    p=0.96  lost=0.85\nBOXED IN, close on all sides, tall     -\u0026gt; brake        p=0.84  risk=1.89\nALL CLEAR, target dead ahead           -\u0026gt; hold_course  p=0.82  risk=0.46\nBRIEF OCCLUSION 0.6s, path clear       -\u0026gt; (muddy, p=0.24)      lost=0.12\n\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/pre\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eThe one muddy case is instructive: the \u003cstrong\u003eChoice\u003c/strong\u003e was unconfident, but the\n\u003cstrong\u003eNoul\u003c/strong\u003e answered it cleanly (\u003ccode\u003etarget_truly_lost=0.12\u003c/code\u003e). So the search\nbehaviour is gated on the Noul, not on the Choice. Use the primitive that\nactually fits the question.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"markdown-heading\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ch3 tabindex=\"-1\" class=\"heading-element\" dir=\"auto\"\u003eThe state has to contain the answer\u003c/h3\u003e\u003ca id=\"user-content-the-state-has-to-contain-the-answer\" class=\"anchor\" aria-label=\"Permalink: The state has to contain the answer\" href=\"#the-state-has-to-contain-the-answer\"\u003e\u003csvg data-component=\"Octicon\" class=\"octicon octicon-link\" viewBox=\"0 0 16 16\" version=\"1.1\" width=\"16\" height=\"16\" aria-hidden=\"true\"\u003e\u003cpath d=\"m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z\"\u003e\u003c/path\u003e\u003c/svg\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eJev initially refused to ever pick \u003ccode\u003eclimb\u003c/code\u003e. That was correct. The state was\nfive horizontal range sectors - it contained no vertical information at all, so\n\"fly over it\" was not an inferable option. Adding the obstruction's top-edge\nheight, whether that top edge is visible to the camera, and the aircraft's own\nclimb ceiling moved \u003ccode\u003eclimb\u003c/code\u003e from never-chosen to p=0.93.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eThat was a state-design bug, not a model failure. It is the single most useful\nthing this project taught.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"markdown-heading\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ch2 tabindex=\"-1\" class=\"heading-element\" dir=\"auto\"\u003eRun it\u003c/h2\u003e\u003ca id=\"user-content-run-it\" class=\"anchor\" aria-label=\"Permalink: Run it\" href=\"#run-it\"\u003e\u003csvg data-component=\"Octicon\" class=\"octicon octicon-link\" viewBox=\"0 0 16 16\" version=\"1.1\" width=\"16\" height=\"16\" aria-hidden=\"true\"\u003e\u003cpath d=\"m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z\"\u003e\u003c/path\u003e\u003c/svg\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"highlight highlight-source-shell notranslate position-relative overflow-auto\" dir=\"auto\" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content=\"./setup.sh                      # venv + fetch the Skydio X2 model\ncp .env.example .env            # then put your key in it\"\u003e\u003cpre\u003e./setup.sh                      \u003cspan class=\"pl-c\"\u003e\u003cspan class=\"pl-c\"\u003e#\u003c/span\u003e venv + fetch the Skydio X2 model\u003c/span\u003e\ncp .env.example .env            \u003cspan class=\"pl-c\"\u003e\u003cspan class=\"pl-c\"\u003e#\u003c/span\u003e then put your key in it\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/pre\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"highlight highlight-source-shell notranslate position-relative overflow-auto\" dir=\"auto\" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content=\"set -a \u0026amp;\u0026amp; . ./.env \u0026amp;\u0026amp; set +a\nexport MUJOCO_GL=glfw           # or egl on a headless box\n\n.venv/bin/python run.py --seconds 65 --seeds 1              # Jev engaged\n.venv/bin/python run.py --no-jev --fast --seconds 65 --seeds 0 1 2   # ablation (free)\n.venv/bin/python run.py --seconds 65 --seeds 1 --video course.mp4    # + telemetry video\nTRACE=1 .venv/bin/python run.py --seconds 65 --seeds 1      # print every judgment\"\u003e\u003cpre\u003e\u003cspan class=\"pl-c1\"\u003eset\u003c/span\u003e -a \u003cspan class=\"pl-k\"\u003e\u0026amp;\u0026amp;\u003c/span\u003e \u003cspan class=\"pl-c1\"\u003e.\u003c/span\u003e ./.env \u003cspan class=\"pl-k\"\u003e\u0026amp;\u0026amp;\u003c/span\u003e \u003cspan class=\"pl-c1\"\u003eset\u003c/span\u003e +a\n\u003cspan class=\"pl-k\"\u003eexport\u003c/span\u003e MUJOCO_GL=glfw           \u003cspan class=\"pl-c\"\u003e\u003cspan class=\"pl-c\"\u003e#\u003c/span\u003e or egl on a headless box\u003c/span\u003e\n\n.venv/bin/python run.py --seconds 65 --seeds 1              \u003cspan class=\"pl-c\"\u003e\u003cspan class=\"pl-c\"\u003e#\u003c/span\u003e Jev engaged\u003c/span\u003e\n.venv/bin/python run.py --no-jev --fast --seconds 65 --seeds 0 1 2   \u003cspan class=\"pl-c\"\u003e\u003cspan class=\"pl-c\"\u003e#\u003c/span\u003e ablation (free)\u003c/span\u003e\n.venv/bin/python run.py --seconds 65 --seeds 1 --video course.mp4    \u003cspan class=\"pl-c\"\u003e\u003cspan class=\"pl-c\"\u003e#\u003c/span\u003e + telemetry video\u003c/span\u003e\nTRACE=1 .venv/bin/python run.py --seconds 65 --seeds 1      \u003cspan class=\"pl-c\"\u003e\u003cspan class=\"pl-c\"\u003e#\u003c/span\u003e print every judgment\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/pre\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eA video run also writes \u003ccode\u003ecourse.mp4.tape.npy\u003c/code\u003e. course.mp4.tape.npy out.mp4 --from 12 --to 30\u003c/pre\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eEvery knob a human should review lives at the top of bugs worth stealing\" href=\"#simulator-bugs-worth-stealing\"\u003e\u003csvg data-component=\"Octicon\" class=\"octicon octicon-link\" viewBox=\"0 0 16 16\" version=\"1.1\" width=\"16\" height=\"16\" aria-hidden=\"true\"\u003e\u003cpath d=\"m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z\"\u003e\u003c/path\u003e\u003c/svg\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eMost of the work was the simulator and the controller, not the model. These all\ncost real time:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cul dir=\"auto\"\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eMuJoCo's \u003ccode\u003emap znear/zfar\u003c/code\u003e are \u003cstrong\u003efractions of \u003ccode\u003estat.extent\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/strong\u003e, not metres. In a\n40 m arena \u003ccode\u003eznear=0.05\u003c/code\u003e blinded the drone inside 1.93 m, so the safety reflex\nnever once fired.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eImage-right is \u003cstrong\u003e-y\u003c/strong\u003e for a camera looking down +x, so the target bearing sign\nwas inverted and the yaw loop became positive feedback: the drone turned\n\u003cem\u003eaway\u003c/em\u003e from what it was chasing.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eThe camera sits inside the airframe, so the drone saw \u003cstrong\u003eits own body\u003c/strong\u003e as an\nobstacle at 3.94 m until own-body geoms were masked out.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eThe target's mast is a separate geom from its hull. Identifying the target by\ngeom instead of by body made the drone avoid its own target.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eClipping negative motor commands destroys thrust \u003cem\u003eand\u003c/em\u003e torque together.\nThrust-priority mixing plus a slew-limited velocity command took peak tilt\nfrom 84 deg (tumble, unrecoverable) to a 40 deg transient.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eAnything you have already climbed over is not a threat. Obstacle pixels have\nto be filtered by height relative to the aircraft, or the reflex shoves you\nback off the wall you just cleared.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eThe geometric attitude controller cannot recover from inverted flight, by\nconstruction.\u003c/strong\u003e Its error term \u003ccode\u003eeR = 0.5*vee(Rd^T R - R^T Rd)\u003c/code\u003e has magnitude\nproportional to \u003cstrong\u003esin(theta)\u003c/strong\u003e: it peaks at 90 deg and falls to \u003cem\u003ezero\u003c/em\u003e at 180 deg,\nso an upside-down aircraft sits at a stationary point with no restoring torque.\nThat is the 179-degree lawn-dart. Swapping it for a quaternion error (magnitude\n\u003ccode\u003esin(theta/2)\u003c/code\u003e, monotonic all the way to 180 deg) gives maximal righting torque\nexactly when it is needed most - verified recovering from 179 deg. This one fix\nalso took the obstacle course from 77 m to 88 m.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eA quadrotor cannot thrust downward, and the controller has to know that.\u003c/strong\u003e On a\nhard commanded descent \u003ccode\u003ea_z + G\u003c/code\u003e goes negative, so the desired thrust axis\n\u003ccode\u003eb3 = a_des/|a_des|\u003c/code\u003e points at the floor and the controller faithfully commands an\nINVERTED attitude. The aircraft flips, drops into attitude recovery (which zeroes\nhorizontal acceleration) and then drifts sideways with no lateral control at all -\nwhile the navigator is still correctly calling for a dodge. Clamping \u003ccode\u003ea_des[2]\u003c/code\u003e\npositive was worth more than every gain-tuning attempt combined.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eLateral control needs a POSITION loop, not a velocity command.\u003c/strong\u003e Commanding a\nlateral velocity and holding it until the next judgment gives the aircraft no notion\nof where to stop: it crosses the whole corridor and buries itself in the far wall.\nAnd the position it servos to has to be \u003cem\u003eestimated\u003c/em\u003e: the wall measurement vanishes\nexactly when it matters (an obstacle fills the view), and a naive \"assume centred\"\nfallback had the aircraft convinced it was mid-tunnel while pinned against a wall at\ny=+5.5 m. Dead-reckon laterally and correct only on plausible wall readings: 0.07 m\nmedian error against ground truth.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eA lost target needs a world-frame estimate, not a bearing.\u003c/strong\u003e A camera\nbearing is meaningless the moment the target leaves frame, so the drone swept\nblindly around a stale heading and sat still while the rover drove away. Fix:\nconvert bearing+range+own pose into a world position, carry it forward with the\nobserved velocity, and fly there. Measured against ground truth the estimate is\ngood to 0.14 m and 0.12 m/s - and it must be differentiated over ~1 s, because\nover one 0.07 s camera frame pixel noise becomes tens of m/s and the drone\nextrapolates itself off the map.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eA reflex must brake for what is in your path, not what is beside you.\u003c/strong\u003e Using\nthe nearest obstacle across the whole forward cone meant walls 1.2 m to either\nside triggered a permanent brake, so any gap narrower than 2x the reflex radius\nwas physically impossible to enter. The gate was not hard, it was forbidden.\nSplitting out \u003ccode\u003epath_ahead_m\u003c/code\u003e (the middle sectors only) fixed it.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eA wide lens helps you \u003cem\u003esee\u003c/em\u003e the target but ruins threat assessment, because\nthings 60 deg off the nose were never in the way. Separate the tracking FOV\nfrom the threat cone.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eRe-applying a heading correction at 50 Hz off a 15 Hz camera applies the same\nerror three times and spins the aircraft. Latch an absolute setpoint per\ncamera frame.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eSim time is not wall-clock time.\u003c/strong\u003e The sim ran 10x real time, so 152 of 182\njudgment requests hit a full queue and the model influenced nothing. If you\nare putting a network call in a control loop, pace the sim to real time or you\nare not testing anything.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"markdown-heading\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ch2 tabindex=\"-1\" class=\"heading-element\" dir=\"auto\"\u003eThe tunnel experiment (\u003ccode\u003etunnel.py\u003c/code\u003e) - partial\u003c/h2\u003e\u003ca id=\"user-content-the-tunnel-experiment-tunnelpy---partial\" class=\"anchor\" aria-label=\"Permalink: The tunnel experiment (tunnel.py) - partial\" href=\"#the-tunnel-experiment-tunnelpy---partial\"\u003e\u003csvg data-component=\"Octicon\" class=\"octicon octicon-link\" viewBox=\"0 0 16 16\" version=\"1.1\" width=\"16\" height=\"16\" aria-hidden=\"true\"\u003e\u003cpath d=\"m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z\"\u003e\u003c/path\u003e\u003c/svg\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eA separate, harder setup: a 620 m enclosed tunnel, 15 obstacles, chasing a car,\nwith \u003cstrong\u003eJev as the only navigator\u003c/strong\u003e - no reflex and no hand-written avoidance at\nall. Two graded \u003ccode\u003eScore\u003c/code\u003e questions (\"how hard to steer, and which way\", \"should it\nchange height\") map straight onto the control command, so the answer \u003cem\u003eis\u003c/em\u003e the\nsteering signal rather than a label to act on.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eMeasured throughput, live in a 500 Hz control loop:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cmarkdown-accessiblity-table\u003e\u003ctable\u003e\n\u003cthead\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003cth\u003e\u003c/th\u003e\n\u003cth\u003e\u003c/th\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003c/thead\u003e\n\u003ctbody\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003edecision latency\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003cstrong\u003e0.118 s\u003c/strong\u003e median, 0.164 s p90\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003esequential ceiling\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e7.4 Hz\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003epipelined (4-6 workers)\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003cstrong\u003e21 decisions/s sustained\u003c/strong\u003e, zero errors in ~2000 calls\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003c/tbody\u003e\n\u003c/table\u003e\u003c/markdown-accessiblity-table\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eThe honest reaction budget at 9 m/s\u003c/strong\u003e: perception 0.03 s, Jev 0.118 s, decision\nage 0.024 s, and the \u003cstrong\u003eairframe 0.70 s to translate 2 m sideways\u003c/strong\u003e. The model is\n13% of the loop; the vehicle is 80%. Making the decisions faster cannot help, and\ncommanding the airframe harder is what makes it tumble.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eStatus: the aircraft is now stable (flies full episodes, never hits the floor,\nrecovers from \u0026gt;90 deg), and in the best runs it dodged with \u003cstrong\u003ezero collisions and\n94% target visibility\u003c/strong\u003e. But it does not reliably clear the whole tunnel - it\ntends to over-commit a dodge and end up against a wall. This is written up as a\npartial result, not a working system.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"markdown-heading\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ch2 tabindex=\"-1\" class=\"heading-element\" dir=\"auto\"\u003eLicense\u003c/h2\u003e\u003ca id=\"user-content-license\" class=\"anchor\" aria-label=\"Permalink: License\" href=\"#license\"\u003e\u003csvg data-component=\"Octicon\" class=\"octicon octicon-link\" viewBox=\"0 0 16 16\" version=\"1.1\" width=\"16\" height=\"16\" aria-hidden=\"true\"\u003e\u003cpath d=\"m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z\"\u003e\u003c/path\u003e\u003c/svg\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eMIT. <p dir="auto">An autonomous quadrotor flies a five-station obstacle course in MuJoCo using
<strong>only its onboard camera</strong>. A small judgment model (<a href="https://typesafe.ai" rel="nofollow">TypeSafe</a>'s
Jev) sits at ~2.5 Hz and decides <em>what the situation means</em>; everything
time-critical stays in ordinary code.</p>
<p dir="auto"><a target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer" href="/RomanSlack/jev-drone/blob/main/docs/climb.png"><img src="/RomanSlack/jev-drone/raw/main/docs/climb.png" alt="climbing over a barrier" style="max-width: 100%;"></a></p>
<p dir="auto">The drone is the Skydio X2 from <a href="https://github.com/google-deepmind/mujoco_menagerie">MuJoCo Menagerie</a></p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li>a real airframe with four rotors, flown by a geometric controller. Nothing
about the flight is scripted.</li>
</ul>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">The idea</h2><a id="user-content-the-idea" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: The idea" href="#the-idea"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">Jev is <strong>not</strong> a vision model. It takes JSON and returns typed answers with
probabilities. So it cannot be the perception layer, and it cannot run at
control rate. What it can do is answer small questions about a situation that
ordinary code finds hard to phrase.</p>
<div class="snippet-clipboard-content notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content=" 500 Hz   geometric controller       flight.Pilot    thrust-priority mixing, slew-limited
  50 Hz   guidance + safety reflex   run.Guidance    ALWAYS owns safety
  15 Hz   camera -&gt; symbolic scene   flight.Eye      depth + segmentation, no ground truth
~2.5 Hz   tactical judgment          tactics.py      Jev, advisory only"><pre class="notranslate"><code> 500 Hz   geometric controller       flight.Pilot    thrust-priority mixing, slew-limited
  50 Hz   guidance + safety reflex   run.Guidance    ALWAYS owns safety
  15 Hz   camera -&gt; symbolic scene   flight.Eye      depth + segmentation, no ground truth
~2.5 Hz   tactical judgment          tactics.py      Jev, advisory only
</code></pre></div>
<p dir="auto">Classical CV turns the depth and segmentation buffers into a compact scene:
five forward range sectors, the height of whatever is blocking the path,
whether its top edge is even visible, and where the target is. Jev reads that
and answers three questions in one call:</p>
<markdown-accessiblity-table><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th>question</th>
<th>type</th>
<th>options</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td><code>maneuver</code></td>
<td><strong>Choice</strong></td>
<td>hold_course / gap_left / gap_right / climb / brake / reacquire</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>risk</code></td>
<td><strong>Score</strong></td>
<td>clear and open -&gt; tight -&gt; about to hit something</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>target_truly_lost</code></td>
<td><strong>Noul</strong></td>
<td>genuinely lost, or just briefly occluded?</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></markdown-accessiblity-table>
<p dir="auto">Code decides <em>when</em> to ask. On an open corridor with the target in view there
is nothing to decide, so no call is made. Scenes are fingerprinted so an
unchanged situation reuses the last judgment. A typical 65 s flight costs about
110 calls.</p>
<p dir="auto"><strong>Code keeps the veto.</strong> A hard reflex layer runs at 50 Hz and overrides any
judgment when something is close. Jev can propose <code>climb</code>, but code refuses it
unless the obstruction's measured top edge is actually within the aircraft's
climb ceiling.</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">The course</h2><a id="user-content-the-course" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: The course" href="#the-course"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">Five stations, each breaking a different assumption:</p>
<ol dir="auto">
<li><strong>Slalom</strong> - ordinary steering around pillars</li>
<li><strong>Low beam</strong> - spans the whole corridor. No lateral gap exists at any width, so "go around" is not available. It must be flown <em>over</em>.</li>
<li><strong>Turnstiles</strong> - arms sweeping across the lane. Moving, must be timed.</li>
<li><strong>Sliding gate</strong> - a 3.2 m gap that slides sideways. Too tall to climb, so it must be threaded.</li>
<li><strong>Cluster</strong> - dense pillars</li>
</ol>
<p dir="auto"><a target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer" href="/RomanSlack/jev-drone/blob/main/docs/chase.png"><img src="/RomanSlack/jev-drone/raw/main/docs/chase.png" alt="chasing through the course" style="max-width: 100%;"></a></p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Results</h2><a id="user-content-results" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Results" href="#results"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">The ablation is the same stack with the Jev call disabled, falling back to a
greedy "steer toward the wider side" heuristic. That baseline is <em>safe but
stuck</em>: it never crashes and it never gets past station 2, because going over
an obstacle is not something it can express.</p>
<markdown-accessiblity-table><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th></th>
<th>baseline (no Jev)</th>
<th>Jev engaged</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td>furthest point reached</td>
<td>17.7 / 17.7 / 17.7 m</td>
<td><strong>77.5 m (whole course)</strong></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>target kept in view</td>
<td>~19%</td>
<td><strong>82%</strong></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>time pinned in reflex</td>
<td>65-71%</td>
<td><strong>9%</strong></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>collisions</td>
<td>0 / 0 / 0</td>
<td><strong>0</strong></td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></markdown-accessiblity-table>
<p dir="auto">The baseline stops dead at station 2 every single time. With Jev the drone
clears the entire course in about 47 s at up to 3.6 m/s:</p>
<div class="snippet-clipboard-content notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="x=19  beam0       t=15.7  z=3.0   climbed over
x=26  turnstiles  t=20.3  z=1.6   timed the sweeping arms
x=38  GATE        t=31.3  z=1.6   threaded the sliding 3.2 m gap
x=44  beam1       t=36.8  z=2.8   climbed over
x=50  cluster     t=41.3  z=1.6   lost the rover in the pillars
x=58  exit        t=46.6          re-acquired it and closed back to 3.7 m"><pre class="notranslate"><code>x=19  beam0       t=15.7  z=3.0   climbed over
x=26  turnstiles  t=20.3  z=1.6   timed the sweeping arms
x=38  GATE        t=31.3  z=1.6   threaded the sliding 3.2 m gap
x=44  beam1       t=36.8  z=2.8   climbed over
x=50  cluster     t=41.3  z=1.6   lost the rover in the pillars
x=58  exit        t=46.6          re-acquired it and closed back to 3.7 m
</code></pre></div>
<p dir="auto"><a target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer" href="/RomanSlack/jev-drone/blob/main/docs/gate.png"><img src="/RomanSlack/jev-drone/raw/main/docs/gate.png" alt="threading the sliding gate" style="max-width: 100%;"></a></p>
<p dir="auto">80 calls over 65 s, 0.11 s median latency, 96k tokens.</p>
<p dir="auto">The cluster is worth noting: the drone genuinely loses the rover there, flies to
where it estimates the rover has got to, and picks it back up. That recovery is
the difference between a demo and a system.</p>
<p dir="auto"><strong>Honest caveats.</strong> The Jev column is a single 65 s run, not a seed-matched
average. On an earlier, simpler arena a matched 3-seed comparison showed <strong>no
advantage</strong> for Jev (it crossed 0/3, same as baseline) - the extra maneuvering
cost target visibility. Run-to-run variance is large. The claim this repo
supports is narrow and specific: <em>the baseline is structurally incapable of the
maneuver, and Jev supplies it.</em> It is not "the model makes the drone better at
everything".</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h3 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">What is and is not the model</h3><a id="user-content-what-is-and-is-not-the-model" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: What is and is not the model" href="#what-is-and-is-not-the-model"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">Worth being precise, because it is easy to overclaim:</p>
<markdown-accessiblity-table><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th>layer</th>
<th>who does it</th>
<th>rate</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td><strong>Awareness</strong> - what is out there, how far, where is the target</td>
<td>numpy on depth + segmentation. <strong>Zero Jev.</strong></td>
<td>15 Hz</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>Flight control - attitude, thrust, mixing</td>
<td>geometric controller. <strong>Zero Jev.</strong></td>
<td>500 Hz</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>Safety reflex - do not hit that</td>
<td>code, and it <strong>overrides</strong> Jev</td>
<td>50 Hz</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><strong>Tactical choice</strong> - over it? around it? which side? is it lost?</td>
<td><strong>100% Jev</strong></td>
<td>~3 Hz</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></markdown-accessiblity-table>
<p dir="auto">Code decides <em>what is there</em>; Jev decides <em>what to do about it</em>. Jev cannot see</p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li>it takes JSON, not pixels. The defensible claim is "a judgment model in a
live control loop at 3 Hz with 0.11 s median latency", not "the model does the
perception".</li>
</ul>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h3 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">The judgments themselves are good</h3><a id="user-content-the-judgments-themselves-are-good" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: The judgments themselves are good" href="#the-judgments-themselves-are-good"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">On hand-built scenes, 6 of 7 correct with strong probabilities:</p>
<div class="snippet-clipboard-content notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="LOW BARRIER, all 5 blocked, top 0.45m  -&gt; climb        p=0.93  risk=1.42
TALL PILLAR ahead, right wide open     -&gt; gap_right    p=0.72  risk=1.53
TALL PILLAR ahead, left wide open      -&gt; gap_left     p=0.40  risk=1.58
TARGET GONE 7s, wide open              -&gt; reacquire    p=0.96  lost=0.85
BOXED IN, close on all sides, tall     -&gt; brake        p=0.84  risk=1.89
ALL CLEAR, target dead ahead           -&gt; hold_course  p=0.82  risk=0.46
BRIEF OCCLUSION 0.6s, path clear       -&gt; (muddy, p=0.24)      lost=0.12"><pre class="notranslate"><code>LOW BARRIER, all 5 blocked, top 0.45m  -&gt; climb        p=0.93  risk=1.42
TALL PILLAR ahead, right wide open     -&gt; gap_right    p=0.72  risk=1.53
TALL PILLAR ahead, left wide open      -&gt; gap_left     p=0.40  risk=1.58
TARGET GONE 7s, wide open              -&gt; reacquire    p=0.96  lost=0.85
BOXED IN, close on all sides, tall     -&gt; brake        p=0.84  risk=1.89
ALL CLEAR, target dead ahead           -&gt; hold_course  p=0.82  risk=0.46
BRIEF OCCLUSION 0.6s, path clear       -&gt; (muddy, p=0.24)      lost=0.12
</code></pre></div>
<p dir="auto">The one muddy case is instructive: the <strong>Choice</strong> was unconfident, but the
<strong>Noul</strong> answered it cleanly (<code>target_truly_lost=0.12</code>). So the search
behaviour is gated on the Noul, not on the Choice. Use the primitive that
actually fits the question.</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h3 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">The state has to contain the answer</h3><a id="user-content-the-state-has-to-contain-the-answer" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: The state has to contain the answer" href="#the-state-has-to-contain-the-answer"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">Jev initially refused to ever pick <code>climb</code>. That was correct. The state was
five horizontal range sectors - it contained no vertical information at all, so
"fly over it" was not an inferable option. Adding the obstruction's top-edge
height, whether that top edge is visible to the camera, and the aircraft's own
climb ceiling moved <code>climb</code> from never-chosen to p=0.93.</p>
<p dir="auto">That was a state-design bug, not a model failure. It is the single most useful
thing this project taught.</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Run it</h2><a id="user-content-run-it" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Run it" href="#run-it"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>

<p dir="auto">A video run also writes <code>course.mp4.tape.npy</code>. Re-cut the visuals from that
without flying again, and without spending any API credits:</p>
<div class="highlight highlight-source-shell notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" dir="auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content=".venv/bin/python replay.py course.mp4.tape.npy out.mp4 --from 12 --to 30"><pre>.venv/bin/python replay.py course.mp4.tape.npy out.mp4 --from 12 --to 30</pre></div>
<p dir="auto">Every knob a human should review lives at the top of <code>tactics.py</code>: the three
questions, the option rubrics, and every threshold that changes how the
aircraft reacts to a judgment.</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Layout</h2><a id="user-content-layout" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Layout" href="#layout"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>

<tr>
<td><code>tactics.py</code></td>
<td><strong>everything Jev-facing</strong>: questions, rubrics, thresholds</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>hud.py</code></td>
<td>telemetry overlay</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>replay.py</code></td>
<td>re-render a recorded flight, no physics, no API calls</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></markdown-accessiblity-table>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Simulator bugs worth stealing</h2><a id="user-content-simulator-bugs-worth-stealing" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Simulator bugs worth stealing" href="#simulator-bugs-worth-stealing"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">Most of the work was the simulator and the controller, not the model. These all
cost real time:</p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li>MuJoCo's <code>map znear/zfar</code> are <strong>fractions of <code>stat.extent</code></strong>, not metres. In a
40 m arena <code>znear=0.05</code> blinded the drone inside 1.93 m, so the safety reflex
never once fired.</li>
<li>Image-right is <strong>-y</strong> for a camera looking down +x, so the target bearing sign
was inverted and the yaw loop became positive feedback: the drone turned
<em>away</em> from what it was chasing.</li>
<li>The camera sits inside the airframe, so the drone saw <strong>its own body</strong> as an
obstacle at 3.94 m until own-body geoms were masked out.</li>
<li>The target's mast is a separate geom from its hull. Identifying the target by
geom instead of by body made the drone avoid its own target.</li>
<li>Clipping negative motor commands destroys thrust <em>and</em> torque together.
Thrust-priority mixing plus a slew-limited velocity command took peak tilt
from 84 deg (tumble, unrecoverable) to a 40 deg transient.</li>
<li>Anything you have already climbed over is not a threat. Obstacle pixels have
to be filtered by height relative to the aircraft, or the reflex shoves you
back off the wall you just cleared.</li>
<li><strong>The geometric attitude controller cannot recover from inverted flight, by
construction.</strong> Its error term <code>eR = 0.5*vee(Rd^T R - R^T Rd)</code> has magnitude
proportional to <strong>sin(theta)</strong>: it peaks at 90 deg and falls to <em>zero</em> at 180 deg,
so an upside-down aircraft sits at a stationary point with no restoring torque.
That is the 179-degree lawn-dart. Swapping it for a quaternion error (magnitude
<code>sin(theta/2)</code>, monotonic all the way to 180 deg) gives maximal righting torque
exactly when it is needed most - verified recovering from 179 deg. This one fix
also took the obstacle course from 77 m to 88 m.</li>
<li><strong>A quadrotor cannot thrust downward, and the controller has to know that.</strong> On a
hard commanded descent <code>a_z + G</code> goes negative, so the desired thrust axis
<code>b3 = a_des/|a_des|</code> points at the floor and the controller faithfully commands an
INVERTED attitude. The aircraft flips, drops into attitude recovery (which zeroes
horizontal acceleration) and then drifts sideways with no lateral control at all -
while the navigator is still correctly calling for a dodge. Clamping <code>a_des[2]</code>
positive was worth more than every gain-tuning attempt combined.</li>
<li><strong>Lateral control needs a POSITION loop, not a velocity command.</strong> Commanding a
lateral velocity and holding it until the next judgment gives the aircraft no notion
of where to stop: it crosses the whole corridor and buries itself in the far wall.
And the position it servos to has to be <em>estimated</em>: the wall measurement vanishes
exactly when it matters (an obstacle fills the view), and a naive "assume centred"
fallback had the aircraft convinced it was mid-tunnel while pinned against a wall at
y=+5.5 m. Dead-reckon laterally and correct only on plausible wall readings: 0.07 m
median error against ground truth.</li>
<li><strong>A lost target needs a world-frame estimate, not a bearing.</strong> A camera
bearing is meaningless the moment the target leaves frame, so the drone swept
blindly around a stale heading and sat still while the rover drove away. Fix:
convert bearing+range+own pose into a world position, carry it forward with the
observed velocity, and fly there. Measured against ground truth the estimate is
good to 0.14 m and 0.12 m/s - and it must be differentiated over ~1 s, because
over one 0.07 s camera frame pixel noise becomes tens of m/s and the drone
extrapolates itself off the map.</li>
<li><strong>A reflex must brake for what is in your path, not what is beside you.</strong> Using
the nearest obstacle across the whole forward cone meant walls 1.2 m to either
side triggered a permanent brake, so any gap narrower than 2x the reflex radius
was physically impossible to enter. The gate was not hard, it was forbidden.
Splitting out <code>path_ahead_m</code> (the middle sectors only) fixed it.</li>
<li>A wide lens helps you <em>see</em> the target but ruins threat assessment, because
things 60 deg off the nose were never in the way. Separate the tracking FOV
from the threat cone.</li>
<li>Re-applying a heading correction at 50 Hz off a 15 Hz camera applies the same
error three times and spins the aircraft. Latch an absolute setpoint per
camera frame.</li>
<li><strong>Sim time is not wall-clock time.</strong> The sim ran 10x real time, so 152 of 182
judgment requests hit a full queue and the model influenced nothing. If you
are putting a network call in a control loop, pace the sim to real time or you
are not testing anything.</li>
</ul>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">The tunnel experiment (<code>tunnel.py</code>) - partial</h2><a id="user-content-the-tunnel-experiment-tunnelpy---partial" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: The tunnel experiment (tunnel.py) - partial" href="#the-tunnel-experiment-tunnelpy---partial"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">A separate, harder setup: a 620 m enclosed tunnel, 15 obstacles, chasing a car,
with <strong>Jev as the only navigator</strong> - no reflex and no hand-written avoidance at
all. Two graded <code>Score</code> questions ("how hard to steer, and which way", "should it
change height") map straight onto the control command, so the answer <em>is</em> the
steering signal rather than a label to act on.</p>
<p dir="auto">Measured throughput, live in a 500 Hz control loop:</p>
<markdown-accessiblity-table><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th></th>
<th></th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td>decision latency</td>
<td><strong>0.118 s</strong> median, 0.164 s p90</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>sequential ceiling</td>
<td>7.4 Hz</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>pipelined (4-6 workers)</td>
<td><strong>21 decisions/s sustained</strong>, zero errors in ~2000 calls</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></markdown-accessiblity-table>
<p dir="auto"><strong>The honest reaction budget at 9 m/s</strong>: perception 0.03 s, Jev 0.118 s, decision
age 0.024 s, and the <strong>airframe 0.70 s to translate 2 m sideways</strong>. The model is
13% of the loop; the vehicle is 80%. Making the decisions faster cannot help, and
commanding the airframe harder is what makes it tumble.</p>
<p dir="auto">Status: the aircraft is now stable (flies full episodes, never hits the floor,
recovers from &gt;90 deg), and in the best runs it dodged with <strong>zero collisions and
94% target visibility</strong>. But it does not reliably clear the whole tunnel - it
tends to over-commit a dodge and end up against a wall. This is written up as a
partial result, not a working system.</p>
